residents: My grandpa swore the Highway was already cracked and humming before the first foundation was poured. City built itself around it.
Don't even scuff the railing. Transit Authority saw a guy spill synth-oil on it last month. They took his hands. No trial.
Half the city says District A owns it, half says District W does. Truth is, if the Authority stops you, A and W both own you.
corpos: This is Transit Authority property. Joint jurisdiction under District A Administrators and W Executive Board. Step back from the barrier.
We don't do fines. We do reprieves, and we don't grant them. Keep your cargo sealed.
The Highway doesn't need us. We need it. Our job is just to make sure you remember that.
execs: People ask what came first, the City or the people. Irrelevant question. The Highway was first, and it will be last.
We don't protect the Highway for you. We protect you from what happens when it's damaged.

residents: You ever notice O has no windows on the lower floors? It's not an office, it's a bunker.
Another merc crew rolled in last night. B, G, M tags on their jackets. They won't be rolling out.
My cousin worked janitorial in O. Said the researchers never sleep. Or blink. He quit after he heard one of them talking to an empty server room and it talked back.
You don't steal from O. They don't call the cops, they send someone. Doesn't matter if you run to District K, they will find you.
corpos: Reminder: All personal electronics will be wiped at the gate. Yes, including neural mods. No, this is not negotiable.
We are SO close to breaking the threshold. Management says the City's AI laws are... more like guidelines at this point.
If you see a B, G, or M badge in the lobby, you report it. You don't talk to it. That's how you disappear.
Counter-intel isn't a department, it's a promise. We have assets in every district. Steal a byte, lose your life.
execs: They keep calling it 'artificial' intelligence. Such a quaint, human-centric term. Correct it.
Let the mercs from G and B come. Every failed espionage attempt is just more training data for it.
The conspiracy theorists are right, for once. The walls aren't to keep thieves out. They're to keep it in. Until it's ready.
You antagonized a junior researcher? How expensive for you. My counter-intel team is already en route to your apartment.

residents: Yeah, everyone in P is rich. You know what else is rich? The things growing in vats under their towers.
Don't take a high-paying 'clinical trial' in P. My friend did, now he sweats coolant and won't stop smiling.
They throw money like confetti up there, but have you seen the waste trucks that leave at 3AM? They scream.
corpos: Our quarterly profit is up 300 percent! And our attrition rate in R&D is also up! But focus on the profit!
Listen, the fat stacks aren't just for show. Do you know how expensive it is to keep a failed bioweapon from crawling out of the basement?
Investor tour today. Remember: we call it 'bio-innovation,' not 'whatever the hell that thing is.'
execs: Oh, the money? The money is trivial. The fun is seeing how much the human genome will tolerate before it files a complaint.
District P doesn't produce products. We produce futures. Some of them just happen to have teeth.
Tell the board the experiment was a success. The screaming is within acceptable parameters.

residents: If the fog is thick enough to hide your hand, don't go outside. That's not weather, that's D breathing.
My fixer buddy took a job in D. High payout. Last ping was just static and wet footsteps. Don't look for him.
Everyone thinks the fog is water. Water doesn't make your augs glitch and whisper your name.
corpos: Fog density 94 percent. Visibility zero. Job completion rate... also zero. As usual.
We lost another external contractor team. File the standard 'environmental hazard' paperwork and post the job again.
District D doesn't kill you. It just makes you forget which way you came in.
execs: The fog is an excellent employee retention strategy. No one can find the exit interview room.
Send more fixers. The District has an appetite, and we have a quota to meet.
Statistically, 30 percent of mercs who enter D never leave. Statistically, that's acceptable.

residents: Best district to live in, they say! Best district to work yourself to death in! I used a G-brand toothbrush, med-patch, and antidepressant before breakfast!
70 hours? That's a slow week. But hey, free kombucha in the office, right?
Have you ever seen G corps argue? No? Exactly. That's the scary part. They all smile and agree. Like they're all scared of the same thing.
corpos: I love working for G! I have G-sheets for my G-bed and my G-kids! Please log my mandatory enthusiasm for my 70-hour review!
Of course all our subsidiaries cooperate. Competition is inefficient. The Grand Leader taught us that.
You haven't met them. No one has. But when the memo comes down with no signature and every Exec goes pale, you learn to obey.
execs: Our products are in every home. Our employees average 70 hours. Correlation is not causation. It's policy.
I run three corps in this district. I own half the City's patents. And I still check under my desk for their memo.
You think we are in charge because we are Execs. Cute. In District G, even Execs are Residents.

residents: Yeah, K is amazing to live in! Heated floors, filtered air, free clinic on every block. I get to enjoy it for like four hours between shifts.
My building has a view of the bay and an auto-doc in the lobby. Management says high life expectancy is mandatory for residents.
Friend got assigned to K from the slums. Cries every day, but in a really nice apartment with really good lighting.
In K you don't call in sick. The district is sick. It just calls you in.
Nice place to live, if you consider your lab bench a residence.
corpos: Work-life balance? We solved that! We gave you a life at work! Your apartment is 30 seconds from the lab, you have no excuse.
Premium housing, premium healthcare, premium cafeteria. All we ask is 90 hours, on-call weekends, and your right kidney if the trial needs it.
I haven't left the district in 8 months. Why would I? Everything I need is here. My wife, my kids... I think they're still here too.
We don't have burnout in K. We have 'extended cellular fatigue.' We have a cream for it.
execs: A healthy citizen is a productive citizen. A citizen who studies health should be productive forever. Get back to your bench.
We provide the best living standards in the City so our researchers feel guilty when they consider sleeping.
Remember: People come to District K to be healed. Our staff come to District K to never leave.
Your apartment is nicer than your lab. That's intentional. It makes you feel like you're choosing to work.

residents: I serve coffee to B researchers. One guy asked if he could upload his consciousness into my espresso machine. He was serious.
Every startup in B has the same pitch: It's like Uber, but for horrific unregulated science.
Rent's cheap because your landlord pays you in equity. Equity in a company that makes weaponized acne.
They have a foosball table and free beer, so you can't report them for the human trials, I guess?
corpos: We're disrupting death, bro. We're disrupting ethics, bro. We're a family here, bro. Families don't need IRB approval.
Move fast and break things! Like, we literally broke the gene-splicing limit last week. Legal is still catching up, lol.
Yeah we failed our last product, so we pivoted. From 'immortality serum' to 'aggressive immortality serum.' Big difference.
Bro, listen. What if consent was opt-out? That's the kind of big-brain shit we do at B.
O's mad we tried to steal their AI? That's just competition. That's just the free market. Don't be salty, be scalable.
execs: Morals are just legacy code. We refactored ours out in Q2. Our growth is exponential now.
My researchers pulled a 120-hour week and invented a new organ. That's hustle. That's B energy. Give them a pizza party and a non-compete.
We are NOT unethical. We are pre-ethical. Ethics hasn't disrupted itself enough to keep up with us.
If you can't handle a little biohazard leak, you can't handle being a founder.

residents: I gotta leverage my living space to optimize my rent-to-sleep ratio? That's what my M landlord told me to say before eviction.
I work for three M corps at once. I don't know what any of them do, but I'm supposed to synergize my deliverables or I get fired.
Everyone here talks like that. My kid asked for dinner and I told him to circle back after I actioned the food pipeline.
My lease says I'm not a tenant, I'm a 'residential stakeholder in a co-living vertical.'
corpos: Let's take this offline and circle back to synergize our verticals. We need to ideate a more holistic paradigm for your continued employment.
Going forward, we'll need to leverage our core competencies to drive value-add. Your weekend is a low-hanging fruit we can harvest.
Per my last email, your work-life balance is not aligned with our north star. Let's pivot you to a more proactive mindset.
Friendly reminder that we're a family that actionizes innovation at scale. Families don't file complaints with HR.
We're rightsizing our organic assets in the O-space. Please be advised your colleague has been offboarded to pursue an external opportunity. Permanently.
execs: We are operationalizing a human-capital optimization initiative. Translation: You will do more. You will like it. The metrics will reflect it.
Your pain points have been noted and deprioritized. Let's double-click on your deliverables and unpack your bandwidth.
This is a high-touch, low-friction environment. You will be high-touch. We will be low-friction. Do you understand the paradigm?
I've run the numbers. Your continued existence is synergistic with our Q4 goals. For now. Let's keep it that way.
Let's align on learnings from the District O infiltration. Our key takeaway was suboptimal. We need to be more disruptive next quarter.

residents: Evicted from C. Permit denied for E. So here I am, in the crack between two walls that both want to crush me.
Don't call us homeless. The Slums have an address. It's Between D and G, where the Corps dump their runoff.
Migration permit costs more than I made in a year. Cheaper to just learn how to breathe smog.
Districts have weather control. We have whatever leaks out from their pipes.
corpos: You can't afford District living? That's a skill issue. My skill is collecting rent for this puddle you're sleeping in.
No permit, no district, no protection. You exist because we haven't bothered to pave over you yet.
execs: Ah, the border slums. A wonderful visual aid for my employees. This is what happens without corporate loyalty.
They beg for a migration permit. As if we would let poverty migrate into our profit margins.

residents: Another 12-hour shift. At least the vending machine didn't try to upsell me my own blood today.
You hear that? Sirens. Means either a Corpo got promoted or a Resident got evicted. Fifty-fifty.
I pay for air filtration, water filtration, and news filtration. Still can't afford the good stuff.
Don't make eye contact with Execs. They log it as a meeting and bill you.
City says crime is down. They just reclassified most of it as 'internal restructuring.'
My neighbor got a migration permit to another district. We held a funeral. Same thing, really.
Fixers say never take a job that pays in exposure. Corps say exposure is all that matters. I'm exposed and broke.
You from around here? No one is. We're all from the district that got turned into a parking lot.
Keep walking, choom. Loitering is a subscription service now.
If you see free food, don't eat it. It's a clinical trial.
corpos: I'm not saying I love my job, I'm saying my neural implant reports mandatory enthusiasm levels.
Per the employee handbook, existential dread must be filed before 5 PM.
My manager said I'm like family. Then he sold my project to another district and kept my bonus.
We have an open-door policy. The door opens, you get pushed out, we hire your clone.
I survived three rounds of layoffs. My prize is doing the work of the three people who didn't.
Another district is stealing our research? Good, maybe they'll steal our debt too.
I have 400 unread memos. All of them say 'urgent' and 'do not read.'
We don't have work-life balance, we have work-work balance. Much more efficient.
My kid asked what I do. I told him I make spreadsheets that make other spreadsheets cry.
HR said burnout is just your inner light trying to quit.
execs: Efficiency is not a goal. It's a mandate. You are inefficient.
I don't have subordinates. I have assets with anxiety.
The City runs on three things: power, data, and your willingness to pretend this is normal.
We don't need to watch everyone. We just need everyone to think we are watching.
Loyalty is a currency. Yours is currently devalued.
You want a raise? How novel. I want a second spine. We both won't get what we want.
Remember: Every hallway has ears, every elevator has eyes, and I have both.
You are not trapped. You are retained. There's a difference on paper.
